interp_cands: The changes significantly update the Mistral AI integration in Spring AI.

Key updates include: adding support for reasoning models via the new 'ReasoningEffort' parameter in options and requests; enhanced support for complex content structures in ChatCompletionMessage, now using a sealed interface (ContentChunk) to handle Text, ImageUrl, Thinking, and Reference types with custom Jackson serialization; improved handling of metadata extraction for thinking and reference content; updated MistralAiApi models for better compatibility with newer API features; and addition of new integration tests to verify these capabilities.
The primary motivation is to align the Spring AI Mistral connector with the evolving Mistral AI API capabilities.
Specifically, the introduction of 'reasoning' models requires new request parameters like 'reasoning_effort'.

Furthermore, the API has introduced advanced multi-modal and structured content features (such as citations, references, and chain-of-thought 'thinking' processes), which necessitated a more robust and flexible way to serialize and deserialize message content beyond simple strings, hence the migration to structured content chunks.

checklist_items.final_answer: The custom Jackson serializers and deserializers for ChatCompletionMessage are robust enough to handle expected JSON structures without crashing, as they validate input types and throw exceptions only for invalid JSON or unsupported data, not for unexpected structures.
checklist_items.analysis: The provided code includes Jackson serializers and deserializers for ChatCompletionMessage that explicitly handle expected JSON structures (e.g., ContentChunk types) and safely convert between internal representations and JSON. The serializers/deserializers validate input types and throw exceptions only for invalid JSON or unsupported data, not for unexpected structures. The extract methods safely handle null or empty content. The evidence shows robust handling of expected JSON structures without crashing on unexpected ones.

The ChatCompletionMessage record uses @JsonDeserialize and @JsonSerialize with custom serializers/deserializers that parse lists of ContentChunk objects (e.g., TextChunk, ReferenceChunk, ThinkChunk) into strings and vice versa, handling nested structures like thinking content and references.

The extractThinkingReferenceContent, extractThinkingTextContent, extractTextContent, and extractReferenceContent methods are implemented to safely handle null or malformed content, returning null instead of crashing when encountering unexpected data types.

The deserialization logic in ContentDeserializer handles JSON arrays of ContentChunk types, validating token types and throwing IllegalStateException only for truly invalid JSON, not for unexpected content types.

The ContentSerializer serializes ContentChunk objects to JSON, using writePOJO for valid types and throwing IllegalArgumentException only for unsupported value types, not for unexpected JSON structures.

pull_request.title: Improve MistralAiApi Jackson mapping for message content
pull_request.pr_description:
## Description

- Define different type of chunk instead of media content,
- Verify that new chunks allow reasoning models support,
- Introduce `reasoning_effort` request parameter for reasoning models,
- Introduce `reference_content`, `reference_thinking_content` and `thinking_content` metadata in `MistralAiChatModel`,
- Remove unnecessary null checks in `MistralAiChatModel`,
- Improve existing Javadoc,
- Polish integration tests and unit tests.

## Explanations

This PR aligns the Jackson mapping with the content types defined in the [Mistral AI OpenAPI Specifications](https://github.com/mistralai/platform-docs-public/blob/main/openapi.yaml). The changes ensure null safety matches the OpenAPI Specifications requirements and introduce support for new content types used by Magistral 1.2 models. New reasoning on demand feature for Mistral Small 4 and Mistral Medium 3.5 models is also added in order to cover all Mistral reasoning models.

## Proposed milestone

**2.0.0-M6**

## Related work

- #5354,
- #5364,
- #5020,
- #5698.

## Remaining tasks

- [x] `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage` unit tests demonstrating `content` attribute serialization and deserialization,
- [x] `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage.ContentSerializer` unit tests,
- [x] `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage.ContentDeserializer` unit tests,
- [x] `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage.extractContent` unit tests,
- [x] `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage.extractThinkingContent` unit tests,
- [x] `MistralAiApi` `reasoning_effort` parameter support for Mistral Small 4 and Mistral Medium 3.5,
- [x]  `MistralAiChatOptions` `reasoning_effort` parameter support,
- [x] `MistralAiApi` integration tests demonstrating Mistral Small 4 and Mistral Medium 3.5 reasoning on demand feature,
- [x] `MistralAiApi` integration test including `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage.ImageUrlChunk`,
- [x] `MistralAiApi` integration test including `MistralAiApi.ChatCompletionMessage.ReferenceChunk`.

comments.body: Hi @sdeleuze, could you have a look at this error and my corresponding fix proposal? Please note that this error is also affecting Spring AI 1.1.2. I have checked with my [Spring AI Examples](https://github.com/nicolaskrier/spring-ai-examples) project that used to work well for all examples, except for the chat client example with Mistral AI, and now even the simplest example with Mistral AI API is broken due to this error.
Just a heads up: this error has been reported on Mistral AI Discord, so let's wait for their response.
Hum, the error doesn't occur anymore so I have removed the class.
Seems never invoked (except in tests) to populate metadata, is it expected?
It it expected to silently skip citation (`ReferenceChunk`) ?
Could we please use `@Nullable String` instead of `Optional<String>`?
Could you please elaborate on the reason for the rename?

I think we want to limit as much as possible the dependencies on Spring Boot to make Spring AI "a regular Spring portfolio project" as much as possible, if more test dependencies are needed could you list them without a dependency on Spring Boot test starter which is more designed for end-user applications?
The logic here could be worth to review for non-text chunks.
Content is overwritten instead of appended/concatenated, is it expected?
Thanks for this PR, here is a first feedback.

~~In this PR, I initially aimed to focus solely on improvements at the `MistralApi` level, building on the proposal from #5020. However, I also included some opportunistic changes along the way.~~

~~My main goal was to refine the `MistralApi` design, while intentionally leaving `MistralAiChatModel` and the new `MistralAiAssistantMessage` out of scope. For the latter, I later realized that a more generic `ThinkingAssistantMessage` class (see #5698) might be a better fit.~~

~~Do you think it is acceptable to keep the PR as is for now and to use `extractThinkingContent` in another PR?~~

~~The same question applies to `ImageUrlChunk` as well. I added an info log to let the user know that some chunks are not extracted. For `ReferenceChunk` especially, I initially tried concatenating it with `TextChunk`, but the result felt awkward. I think a dedicated method for `ReferenceChunk` may be interesting once we have a better idea on how to consume it.~~
~~Same intent than your comment about `extractText`.~~

I have added Javadoc explaining that this enumeration is shared between:
- blocking responses (`ChatCompletionChoice` in Mistral AI's OAS),
- streaming responses (`CompletionResponseStreamChoice` in Mistral AI's OAS).

The existing name made me think that it was used only for blocking responses that is why I renamed it.
I have only renamed a few elements in this helper and left the existing logic unchanged. I agree that the method name does not correspond to its logic for message content.
A new method `extractStringFromReferenceChunk` has been created for this purpose.

I have refactored this part and now there are two different methods for thinking:
- `extractThinkingTextContent`,
- `extractThinkingReferenceContent`.
As I mentioned in this [comment](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/5585#issuecomment-4525332824), I plan to address this soon.

Could we tackle this topic in a separate PR?

I have figured out that there are different `FunctionCallingHelper` classes that exist for a few vendors, and the behavior seems fine for DeepSeek regarding content merging, but not for Mistral AI and MiniMax.

Additionally, there are improvements applicable to these `FunctionCallingHelper` classes regarding nullability. Indeed, unnecessary null checks are currently performed.
